groups: Ten existing output types with the declared exception population
Preview profiles bound permitted records and permitted actions
Technician scope excludes commercial, project and restricted records
Content identity is computed from the exact encoded bytes
A missing exact item has no bytes, no identity and no substitute
Preparation and issue times are distinct on every retained issue
Owned follow-up is prepared once per exact target and changes no fixture
Read-only and recipient profiles cannot change issue or distribution records
A successor needs a definition, a reason and no existing draft
An independent domain reviewer records the decision against the exact basis
An unconfigured release rule cannot produce a Checked decision
A changed source blocks the successor release until the basis is refreshed
A Checked decision requires every other readiness check to be met
Preparation reserves an identity, verifies bytes and is interrupted once
An unknown finalisation outcome is an owned exception and refuses release
Recovery continues the original operation without regenerating bytes
Release commits one issue with separate preparation and issue times
Repeating the original operation returns the same issue result
The predecessor keeps its exact bytes, recipients and responses
A changed bundle item creates a successor set while the earlier set stays exact
Distribution requires an approved recipient on a current issue
Restricted Finance evidence and internal cost content refuse an external route
A channel without delivery evidence cannot record Delivered
Per-recipient results are independent and an unknown outcome is never repeated
Reconciliation is additive and retains the original attempt evidence
Acknowledgement binds the exact presentation and stays with its own issue
Withdrawal retains the exact issue and its recorded reason
A stale saved version refuses a write without mutating state
Malformed saved state and altered evidence are rejected
Export honours the preview scope and states that nothing was delivered
A retained response records its binding over the whole presented set
A reconciliation cannot establish Delivered on a channel with no delivery evidence
The released issue carries the domain stated purpose, not the draft proposal
Actual issue time must be later than the reserved preparation time
A returned successor can be replaced and both decisions are retained
A response cannot be recorded against a superseded or withdrawn issue
Only the issue in force can be withdrawn
The issue-state filter finds superseded and withdrawn issues
